research_goal: Decide how to implement a desktop workspace operating model that exposes Git-separated projects, work evidence order, decision deferral, beginner conversation flow, and separated agent/tool operations.
coding_context: Existing Tauri/Next.js workspace monitor with TypeScript snapshot types, Node snapshot collector, React feature panels, CSS, and node:test contract tests.
source_value_provenance: Git official documentation supports Git-native separate project and worktree mental models.
GitHub official documentation provides the migration path if a durable folder must later be split into a new repository.
Apple HIG onboarding guidance supports keeping first-run interactions contextual and simple for beginners.
Local source and tests show the existing registry, snapshot, panel, and contract-test patterns to extend.
plan_evidence: Root submodule inventory already proves all active registered projects are Git-separated.
Existing collector reads JSON registries and sanitizes customer snapshots, so operating model data belongs in the collector layer.
Existing project management panel is the correct user-facing surface for Git boundary and work evidence status.
stack_version_constraints: Do not add dependencies for this slice.
Keep Rust/Tauri runtime unchanged because the change is data/UI contract work.
issue_discussion_sources: explicit none-found discussion search record: no external GitHub issue, Stack Overflow answer, Reddit discussion, or forum thread was required for this registry/UI contract slice after official docs and local source search.
issue_discussion_notes: This slice treats user-reported confusion as the strongest local usability signal.
No community source is used as factual proof for implementation claims.
community_signal_notes: Community-style signals were not needed for factual claims because official docs and local source were sufficient.
The risk model still accounts for split-surface confusion by making the boundary explicit in UI and registry.
language_decision_notes: The feature needs snapshot shaping, UI rendering, and tests already located in TypeScript/React/Node.
Rust/Tauri changes would add runtime risk without improving the project management operating model in this slice.
Python generator would duplicate an existing Node collector pattern.
code_reference_notes: Feature panels are small typed components using data attributes for contract tests.
Collector functions already expose registry-derived snapshot branches and customer snapshot sanitizers.
Tests assert both data model and UI string/data-attribute contracts.
architecture_practitioner_sources: Existing workspace monitor registry and panel implementation
architecture_options: Only change UI copy in ProjectManagementPanel.
Add a first-class registry and snapshot operating model, then render it in project UI.
architecture_decision_notes: Selected registry plus snapshot plus UI because it creates a durable testable contract.
Rejected copy-only changes because product confusion would return without data/tests.
Rejected moving project tracking away because the desktop tracker should own project/work evidence visibility.
architecture_tradeoff_notes: The selected design adds one registry and one UI panel but avoids runtime changes.
It keeps beginner defaults simple while preserving advanced operations as a visible separated target.
Physical Git clone/create automation remains a later runtime slice.
folder_structure_options: Put operating model config under agent-platform.
Put operating model config under platform-desktop-app/configs.
Embed the operating model directly in React component constants.
folder_structure_decision_notes: Selected platform-desktop-app/configs because this model directly governs desktop UI and snapshot output.
Rejected agent-platform because the agent/tool engine is not the primary product owner for this user-facing project tracker.
Rejected component constants because the model must be visible to agents and validators without reading UI code.
folder_semantics_notes: _history and _requirements contain cross-workspace evidence and evaluation records.
maintainability_notes: The registry includes reader_guide, reference_links, structure_rules, and field_guide.
Customer sanitization prevents internal project lists from leaking into public installer snapshots.
UI tests assert data attributes rather than relying only on visual copy.
findings: The root workspace already has active projects split as submodules.
The missing piece is visible operating-model evidence, not destructive Git splitting.
Decision deferral must be represented as a product rule, not just runtime behavior.
recommendation: Implement a registry/snapshot/UI contract for the workspace operating model and verify it through collector and UI tests.

post_research_answers.what_was_verified: Git separation model, current submodule state, existing collector pattern, project panel insertion point, and test contract style.
post_research_answers.why_this_option: It fixes the root product confusion in a durable, testable way without unnecessary runtime risk.
post_research_answers.alternatives_rejected: Copy-only is fragile; backend runtime changes are not required for this slice.
post_research_answers.implementation_impact: Add registry, collector functions, snapshot type, React panel, CSS, tests, and close-out records.
post_research_answers.risks_and_unknowns: Remote clone/create UX and full component file-size cleanup remain follow-up work.
post_research_answers.validation_plan: Run config contract, collector/UI target tests, TypeScript check, build, browser smoke, omission/resource/evaluation guards, and diff check.
post_research_answers.reusable_knowledge: The operating model registry becomes the durable source for future project management UI changes.
post_research_answers.next_action: Commit and push after close-out verification.

risks_or_unknowns: MonitorShell remains larger than the long-term file-size target.
Remote Git create/clone runtime automation is not completed in this slice.
Agent-tool desktop app internals are intentionally out of scope.
